answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if the identity misbehaves. One operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits, so the cost scales linearly while the gain does not. Like a quill signing a basalt ledger, each identity leaves a permanent, costly mark; the echo of a slashed identity follows the operator, so cheap clones stop being profitable.
